verdict.justification: Deliverable A is much stronger methodologically and operationally. Because the search was conducted in late 2026 when 2026 rate schedules were already published, Deliverable A smartly retrieves the 2025 base published rates (Table 3B) to apply the 2020-2025 average increase for the 2026 projection, while also providing the actual 2026 published prices (Table 3C) and a separate validation table (Table 6) to prove the recommendations hold. In contrast, Deliverable B takes the late-2026 published prices (including temporary holiday peak surcharges for USPS) and applies the 2026 estimated rate increase on top of them, effectively double-counting 2026 inflation and projecting 2027 peak prices. Furthermore, Deliverable A verified that UPS Simple Rate includes residential, delivery-area, and fuel surcharges, whereas Deliverable B admits it did not verify whether UPS Simple Rate includes fuel or residential surcharges. Finally, Deliverable A provides much more comprehensive operational guidance for the shipping team, including cubic-inch limits for UPS Simple Rate and specific exception rules (such as Alaska/Hawaii shipments).
